rationale:
Correction to the initial response: there is no ~1e-6 m scatter and no stochastic spread here. The earliest same-condition/shared-input discrepancy is deterministic and larger than I first stated: over the shared 0.00–0.01 interval with held input and the identical recorded tensions (shared identity 661f70b2…), the coarse (0.01 s) reproduction error versus the recorded backend is 0.0004143777671856278 m (0.414378 mm) position and 0.05408022096219525 m/s velocity-vector error. Own-backend command separation starts at 0.02 s; inter-weight preview separation starts at 0.20 s. These are distinct saved timestamps, not the same event and not merely transient scales.

Under refinement of that one shared integration, the earliest velocity-vector discrepancy is substantially reduced: backend vector error falls from 0.0540802 to 0.0100556 m/s at the finest tested (3.125e-5 s) step — absolute reduction 0.0440246 m/s, relative 0.8141. Successive halving differences decay roughly first-order, ~2:1 — position 1.50e-5, 7.65e-6, 3.86e-6, 1.94e-6 m; speed 1.905e-3, 9.678e-4, 4.879e-4, 2.449e-4 m/s; velocity 1.926e-3, 9.788e-4, 4.934e-4, 2.477e-4 m/s (measured uncertainty ≈1.94e-6 m; ≈2.45e-4 m/s speed/velocity). Ratios near two, not collapse, mean the error stays step-dominated rather than asymptotic. The coarse speed error (−0.0539631 m/s) crosses zero to +0.003353 m/s at the finest step while position error plateaus near 5.045e-5 m and speed error slightly grows in the last halving: the finest tested endpoint is not a supported reference, and its residual is not a stabilized physical error.

Instantaneous projected observed output versus the actual backend differs: projected position [0.297928, 0.001161, 0.151140] m and speed 0.247958 m/s against backend [0.297898, 0.001503, 0.151706] m and 0.227942 m/s (position gap ≈6.62e-4 m; speed gap ≈0.0200 m/s). The ordered identity total = evolution + instantaneous projection term: at 0.01 s evolution norm 0.020682, projection-output norm 0.034071, total 0.054080 — components partially cancel, so the total sits below the norm sum and cannot be apportioned to one term. The instantaneous output term is state-coupled and does not by itself identify a projection bug; coupled state/input histories and order dependence forbid causal percentages.

Three levels must be separated. Local numerical self-consistency: same-shared-input refinements show finite, verified root residuals and small measured uncertainty, but convergence is still first-order and the supplied result marks numerical stability unresolved. Backend agreement: even the finest tested reproduction retains ≈0.01006 m/s vector and ≈5.05e-5 m position error versus the plant — unresolved. Full-history screening: the earlier retrospective screen abstained, so this single interval says nothing about prospective discrimination.

Costs: first-interval complete costs grow ≈7.2 → 4.7 → 9.3 → 18.6 → 37.5 → 74.6 s with halving; the deferred weight preview (694.4 s) already exceeds complete evaluation (605.9 s). The incumbent is accurate (terminal 0.00270 m; sampled settling passed 0.00273 m / 0.01275 m/s) but not real-time (35/35 deadline misses; mean update 8.5 s; real_time_demonstrated=false).
